CONTEXT_vs_ARM-TAG.note: no discordant pairs; arms agree on every run

CONTEXT_vs_ARM-DIGEST.note: no discordant pairs; arms agree on every run

CONTEXT_vs_GLOBAL.reason: material FPR reduction achieved, significant after Holm correction, recall non-inferior

limitations: TAG and DIGEST are indistinguishable in this dataset: every human_tag maps to exactly one digest, so no tag-repoint (mutable alias pointing to a different build) scenario has been tested.

Sample size (n=35 benign, n=62 scenario) is well below the frozen protocol full matrix (30 benign + 20 scenario per workload-variant cell = 200 total); this is a first confirmatory-eligible result, not the final powered study.
ART-DES-001 sample-size lock has not been generated; this analysis was not power-planned in advance, it analyses the data actually collected.
Only 2 attack-like scenarios tested (CVE-2021-44228 log4shell-shaped, CVE-2019-5736 runc-escape-shaped), both are simulated harmless process shapes, not real exploits.
Detection here is JS-distance-threshold based (matching the production scorer), not the full POR-DET-* rule-based detection layer; the two are complementary, not identical.

tag_drift_experiment.mechanism: porygon-study/nginx:mutable local alias, repointed from WL-NGX-V1 (nginx:1.26.3-alpine) to WL-NGX-V2 (nginx:1.28.0-alpine) between fit and drift phases, per PROFILE_SCOPE_EXPERIMENT_V1.md Immutable workload coordinates section
tag_drift_experiment.finding: process_name-level Jensen-Shannon distance between the pooled V1 and pooled V2 distributions is exactly 0.0 at n=8+8. nginx 1.26.3-alpine and 1.28.0-alpine produce byte-identical process-name shapes in their docker-entrypoint.sh startup sequence for this workload/mode.
tag_drift_experiment.interpretation: This is a real, honest limitation of process-name-level detection, not a bug in the tag-drift mechanism (which correctly resolves the same human_tag to two verifiably different image digests, confirmed per-trial). A patch/minor-version upgrade that does not change the entrypoint script or which binaries execute is invisible to this signal. ARM-TAG vs ARM-DIGEST therefore remain statistically indistinguishable for this specific real-world drift scenario, though for a different reason than before (now a genuine negative result under a real test, not an untested gap).
tag_drift_experiment.implication: A tag-repoint attack/version-drift scenario that changes deeper behaviour (e.g. a config default, a new startup script, an added executable) would likely still be caught; a same-behaviour patch upgrade would not be, by this feature alone. This argues for combining process-name distance with other signals (e.g. image_config_hash, executable path set, numeric event-rate features already computed by the production scorer) rather than relying on process-name JS distance in isolation for detecting tag drift specifically.
